test_meta.title: ST – Practice Set D: Surgical Anatomy & Procedural Steps

questions.stem: During a laparoscopic cholecystectomy, which two anatomical structures must be positively identified, double-clipped, and divided prior to removing the gallbladder from the liver bed?
options: Common bile duct and hepatic artery
Portal vein and common hepatic duct
Falciform ligament and left gastric artery
questions.explanation: The Critical View of Safety requires dissecting Calot's triangle until only two structures enter the gallbladder: the cystic duct and the cystic artery.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 16, pg 504

questions.stem: What small, blind-ended lymphatic organ arises from the posteromedial wall of the cecum approximately 2 cm below the ileocecal valve?
questions.explanation: The vermiform appendix arises from the cecum where the three taeniae coli converge on the posteromedial cecal wall.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 16, pg 488

questions.stem: Which anatomical structure carries sperm from the epididymis through the inguinal canal into the ejaculatory duct, and is isolated and transected during a vasectomy?
questions.explanation: The vas deferens is the muscular tube coursing within the spermatic cord that propels spermatozoa from the epididymis to the prostatic urethra.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 19, pg 584

questions.stem: During open inguinal hernia repair, which anatomical layer of the spermatic cord is incised longitudinally to expose the indirect hernia sac?
questions.explanation: The spermatic cord is enveloped by external spermatic fascia, cremasteric muscle/fascia, and internal spermatic fascia; opening the cremasteric fibers exposes the anteromedial hernia sac.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 16, pg 484

questions.stem: Which retroperitoneal endocrine glands sit like caps atop the superior poles of each kidney and produce adrenaline, aldosterone, and cortisol?
questions.explanation: The adrenal glands reside in Gerota's fascia above each kidney; the cortex secretes steroid hormones (aldosterone/cortisol) and the medulla secretes catecholamines (epinephrine).
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 19, pg 579

questions.stem: Which vessel is clamped first during carotid endarterectomy to prevent embolization of plaque fragments into the cerebral circulation?
questions.explanation: The internal carotid artery (ICA) is clamped first so that any micro-thrombi loosened during surgical manipulation are diverted harmlessly into the external carotid circulation rather than the brain.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 21, pg 633

questions.stem: In coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery, which in-situ arterial graft is harvested from the anterior chest wall to revascularize the left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery?
questions.explanation: The Left Internal Mammary Artery (LIMA) is the conduit of choice for LAD bypass due to its superior long-term patency exceeding 90% at 10 years.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 22, pg 664

questions.stem: What is the primary anatomical landmark for identifying the recurrent laryngeal nerve during thyroid lobectomy?
options: Tracheoesophageal groove and inferior thyroid artery crossing
questions.explanation: The recurrent laryngeal nerve ascends within the tracheoesophageal groove, closely related to the branches of the inferior thyroid artery before entering the larynx.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 15, pg 462

questions.stem: Which anatomical joint in the human body is classified as a ball-and-socket synovial joint with the greatest range of multi-axial motion?
questions.explanation: The glenohumeral joint is a ball-and-socket joint that permits flexion, extension, abduction, adduction, circumduction, and rotation, sacrificing skeletal stability for mobility.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 20, pg 597

questions.stem: In total knee arthroplasty (TKA), which major knee ligament is routinely sacrificed during bone resection and replaced by the prosthetic polyethylene tibial insert?
questions.explanation: The anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) is excised during tibial and femoral plateau preparation in standard total knee replacements; the posterior cruciate may be preserved or sacrificed.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 20, pg 612

questions.stem: Which cranial meningeal layer is the tough, fibrous, outermost membrane lining the interior of the cranium and forming the falx cerebri and tentorium cerebelli?
questions.explanation: The dura mater ('tough mother') is the thickest, outermost protective meningeal layer adhering directly to the inner table of cranial bones.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 23, pg 682

questions.stem: During craniotomy, where does cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) circulate between the delicate middle and inner meningeal layers?
questions.explanation: CSF flows continuously through the subarachnoid space situated between the arachnoid membrane and the underlying pia mater that clings to cerebral convolutions.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 23, pg 683

questions.stem: Which long bone in the lower extremity is the non-weight-bearing lateral stabilizer commonly harvested for vascularized fibular autografts in mandible or spine reconstruction?
questions.explanation: The fibula bears minimal axial skeletal weight (<15%), making its mid-shaft and peroneal vascular pedicle ideal for composite microvascular bony autografts.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 20, pg 602

questions.stem: What is the primary anatomical landmark used to localize the transverse colon during exploratory laparotomy?
options: The greater omentum attached along its anterior surface and the three longitudinal taeniae coli bands
questions.explanation: The large intestine is recognized by three longitudinal muscle bands (taeniae coli), sacculations (haustra), epiploic fatty appendages, and the attached greater omentum on the transverse colon.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 16, pg 493

questions.stem: During a cesarean section delivery, what transverse lower abdominal incision through skin and subcutaneous fat along the Pfannenstiel line is standard?
questions.explanation: The Pfannenstiel incision is a curved transverse incision made 2-3 cm above the pubic symphysis along natural skin lines, offering superior cosmetic healing and fascial strength.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 18, pg 552

questions.stem: Which incision provides optimal open surgical exposure to the gallbladder, liver, and biliary tree in the right upper quadrant?
questions.explanation: The right subcostal (Kocher) incision parallels the right costal margin 2 cm below the ribs, offering direct visualization of the liver, gallbladder, and biliary ductal system.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 16, pg 500

questions.stem: Which anatomical structure separates the thoracic cavity from the abdominopelvic cavity and functions as the primary skeletal muscle of inspiration?
questions.explanation: The diaphragm is a dome-shaped musculotendinous partition separating thorax and abdomen, innervated by the phrenic nerves (C3, C4, C5).
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 22, pg 646

questions.stem: Which three structures pass through distinct openings in the diaphragm?
options: Inferior vena cava (T8), Esophagus (T10), and Aorta (T12)
Trachea, Carotid artery, and Jugular vein
Femoral artery, Femoral vein, and Saphenous nerve
Celiac axis, Renal artery, and Ureter
questions.explanation: The three major diaphragmatic hiatuses are: caval opening (T8) for IVC, esophageal hiatus (T10) for esophagus and vagus nerves, and aortic hiatus (T12) for descending aorta and thoracic duct.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 16, pg 475

questions.stem: What is the primary anatomical function of the spleen in human immunology and hematology?
options: Filtering aged senescent erythrocytes, storing platelets, and mounting IgM antibody immune responses against encapsulated bacteria
Secreting digestive enzymes into the duodenum
questions.explanation: The spleen's red pulp filters old RBCs and debris; its white pulp contains lymphoid follicles producing antibodies against encapsulated pathogens (Pneumococcus, Meningococcus).
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 16, pg 515

questions.stem: During an open abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) repair, which major renal vessels crossing anterior to the aorta must be mobilized to safely place the proximal aortic cross-clamp?
questions.explanation: The left renal vein crosses anteriorly over the abdominal aorta directly beneath the origin of the SMA; mobilizing it is crucial for exposing the infrarenal aortic neck.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 21, pg 636

questions.stem: In ophthalmology, what is the clear, circular, avascular anterior portion of the fibrous outer tunic of the eye that refracts light into the pupil?
questions.explanation: The cornea is the transparent anterior window of the eye that accounts for roughly two-thirds of the optical refractive power, receiving oxygen directly from air and tears.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 14, pg 444

questions.stem: During cataract extraction (phacoemulsification), what cloudy, opaque natural anatomical structure is fragmented and replaced by an artificial intraocular lens (IOL)?
questions.explanation: A cataract is an opacification of the natural biconvex crystalline lens of the eye; phacoemulsification uses ultrasonic energy to break it apart inside the capsular bag.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 14, pg 448

questions.stem: Which anatomical ossicle in the middle ear is shaped like a stirrup and connects the incus to the oval window of the cochlea?
questions.explanation: The three auditory ossicles are Malleus, Incus, and Stapes. The stapes footplate vibrates against the oval window fluid of the inner ear.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 17, pg 524

questions.stem: In ENT surgery, which surgical procedure involves creating a microscopic opening in the tympanic membrane to suction middle ear fluid and insert pressure-equalizing (PE) tubes?
questions.explanation: Myringotomy (tympanostomy) is an incisional slit made in the inferior quadrant of the eardrum to ventilate the middle ear space and place PE tubes for chronic otitis media.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 17, pg 526

questions.stem: Which major salivary gland is the largest, located anterior and inferior to the external ear canal, and produces watery serous saliva transmitted through Stensen's duct?
questions.explanation: The parotid gland is the largest salivary gland, draining via Stensen's duct into the oral vestibule opposite the second upper molar.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 17, pg 530

questions.stem: During lumbar laminectomy for herniated disc removal, which yellow, elastic ligament connecting the laminae of adjacent vertebrae is incised to enter the spinal canal?
questions.explanation: The ligamentum flavum ('yellow ligament') connects adjacent vertebral laminae; surgeons excise it to expose the underlying thecal sac and nerve roots.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 23, pg 686

questions.stem: What is the primary anatomical function of the meniscus fibrocartilage pads in the human knee joint?
options: Shock absorption, load distribution, and deepening the tibial articulating surface for the femoral condyles
Connecting the patella to the fibula
questions.explanation: The medial and lateral crescent-shaped menisci act as shock absorbers that disperse 50-70% of compressive axial loads and lubricate the knee joint.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 20, pg 601

questions.stem: Which ligament in the ankle is the most commonly torn ligament in inversion ankle sprains and sports reconstructions?
questions.explanation: The Anterior Talofibular Ligament (ATFL) spans from the lateral malleolus to the talus neck and is the primary lateral stabilizer injured during hyper-inversion trauma.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 20, pg 603

questions.stem: In urology, what is the triangular smooth anatomical region of the bladder floor bounded by the bilateral ureteral orifices and the internal urethral meatus?
questions.explanation: The trigone is a smooth triangular mucosal area at the bladder base formed between the two ureteric openings superiorly and the internal urethral sphincter inferiorly.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 19, pg 581

questions.stem: Which major abdominal vein is formed by the union of the superior mesenteric vein and the splenic vein, carrying nutrient-rich deoxygenated blood to the liver for metabolic processing?
questions.explanation: The hepatic portal vein forms behind the pancreatic neck by the confluence of the splenic vein and superior mesenteric vein, conducting blood to hepatic sinusoids.
questions.source_ref: AST Core Curriculum 6th Ed., Ch. 16, pg 505
